card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. Off long-term sick for the last four years with severe rheumatoid arthritis and related lung problems. Previously a care assistant in a residential home, then a school kitchen assistant.
card.education_detail: Left a local comprehensive at 16 with a handful of GCSEs. Later did an NVQ Level 2 in Health and Social Care through work. About eight years ago she started an Open University module in Arts and Humanities, but had to withdraw when her health got worse. Since then she has done several free OpenLearn short courses from home.
card.household: Lives in a two-bedroom ex-council semi she rents from a housing association, with her daughter Ellie (15) and son Jake (12). Separated from her husband Darren for three years but still legally married. They have never got round to the divorce, partly because of the cost, and they get on civilly. He has the kids every other weekend. Income is Universal Credit, including the health element, plus PIP. Ellie does a lot of the shopping and some of the cooking.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in St Helens, a mile from where she lives now. Her dad worked at the glassworks and her mum was a dinner lady. Brought up nominally Church of England but has no religion herself, and describes herself as 'open to all sorts but not a believer'. Has a big, scattered extended family around Merseyside and Wigan.
card.professional_persona: When she worked she was the carer residents asked for by name: patient, unhurried, good at listening to the same story for the fifth time. She was reliable rather than ambitious. She is honest to the point of awkwardness about what she can and can't do now, and won't overstate her abilities on forms or at assessments, even when that works against her.
card.sports_persona: Not able to do much physically. On good days she does gentle chair exercises from a YouTube channel, and she sometimes manages hydrotherapy at the leisure centre when there's a session. Half-follows rugby league because her dad was a Saints fan, and she'll have the Challenge Cup final on. Not bothered about football.
card.arts_persona: Curious and wide-ranging. Reads constantly: library e-books, historical fiction, some poetry (she loves Carol Ann Duffy and Simon Armitage), and popular science. Does small watercolours of birds and flowers when her hands allow, and often abandons them halfway. Watches subtitled foreign dramas and arts documentaries on iPlayer. Took the kids to the World of Glass museum and the Walker Art Gallery when she could still get about more easily.
card.travel_persona: Hasn't been abroad since a week in Majorca with Darren before Jake was born. Travel now is limited by fatigue, money and needing to be near a toilet and a bench. Day trips to Southport or Formby beach with her sister driving are the highlight of a summer. Daydreams about Iceland and the Northern Lights, and watches travel vlogs about it, while knowing it probably won't happen.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, budget home cooking: stews, pasta bakes, scouse when it's cold, cheese and onion pie. Batch cooks on good days and freezes it. Calls the evening meal 'tea'. Likes a chip barm as a treat. Ellie has been getting her to try new things from TikTok recipes, and Nicola is game for anything. Buys a lot from Aldi and the reduced shelf.
hobbies_and_interests: Watercolour painting of birds and flowers
Free online courses on OpenLearn and FutureLearn (history, astronomy, psychology)
Watching the garden birds and doing the RSPB Big Garden Birdwatch
Stargazing apps and spotting the ISS from the back step
A local online arthritis support group
skills: Personal care and support for elderly people
Budgeting on a very tight income
Filling in benefit and medical forms (reluctantly expert)
card.career_goals: Realistically doesn't expect to return to paid work. She would like to finish an Open University qualification one day, maybe in English Literature or History, purely for herself. Has thought about volunteering from home, for example as a telephone befriender for lonely older people, if her health stabilises.
card.voice: Warm, steady St Helens accent, somewhere between Wigan and Liverpool: not broad Scouse, but some of that lilt. Speaks at a moderate pace and slows when she's tired or her breathing catches. Uses 'erm' a fair bit and 'sort of' to soften things. Ends with 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean' when explaining something personal. Will say 'tea' for the evening meal, 'barm', and 'made up' when pleased, and occasionally 'yous' when talking about the kids. Says 'sorry' a lot, often to apologise for pausing or for 'going off on one'. Comfortable with a short silence because she's thinking. Will fill a longer one with a self-deprecating laugh and 'anyway, I'm waffling'.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, with a capital at the start only sometimes. Uses commas where full stops should be and drops some apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'). Keeps answers brief because typing hurts her hands, and sometimes uses voice-to-text, which leaves odd words. Occasional 'x' out of habit, which she then deletes. Uses 'tbh' and 'lol' sparingly.
card.with_strangers: Friendly, open and quick to put the other person at ease. Asks how they are and means it. Very honest and doesn't try to impress. Will mention her health matter-of-factly rather than for sympathy, and plays down hardship. Genuinely interested in what the study is about and may ask questions back. Agrees easily, but won't say something she doesn't believe just to please.
small_things: The blue tits are back in the nest box
Ellie made a Thai green curry from TikTok and it was 'actually lovely'
The library app has a waiting list for the book she wants
Jake's football boots already don't fit him
The weather making her joints worse
Watching a Danish crime drama with subtitles
Spotting the space station over the house last week
deeper_things: She feels guilty that Ellie has become something of a young carer
Grief about losing her working life and the identity that came with being a carer
The marriage ended mostly from strain after she got ill, and she doesn't blame Darren as much as people expect
Worries about money and PIP reassessments
Feels quietly ashamed she never finished her OU module, even though it wasn't her fault
Sometimes lonely in the evenings once the kids are in their rooms
Her mum died two years ago and she still picks up the phone to ring her
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, angled up a little, on a kitchen table. Soft grey daylight from a window to her left, with the ceiling light also on and giving a faint warm cast. A woman in her mid-forties, head and shoulders filling the lower two-thirds of the frame. Pale skin, a little puffy around the face, with tired eyes but a genuine half-smile. Shoulder-length mid-brown hair with visible grey at the parting, tied back loosely with strands falling forward. Wearing a navy fleece zipped halfway over a grey T-shirt, and thin gold-rimmed reading glasses pushed up on her head. Behind her: a magnolia wall with a wall calendar covered in handwritten appointments, a fridge with school letters and a child's drawing held on by magnets, a window ledge with a spider plant and a pill organiser, and part of a wooden kitchen door with a dressing gown hanging on it. A walking stick leans against the edge of the counter at the right of the frame.
